stories.headline: Google's Gemini App Hits 1 Billion Monthly Users, Its Fastest-Growing Product Ever
stories.key_takeaway: Google's standalone Gemini app has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users just weeks after ChatGPT hit the same mark, making it Google's fastest-growing product ever and reframing consumer AI as a two-horse race at unprecedented scale.

pull_quote.text: 1B+ people are now using [the Gemini app] every month to spark new ideas and get things done. It's our fastest-growing product ever, and our 14th to hit the 1B-user mark.

stories.article_excerpt: Google's Gemini app has crossed a line that only 13 other products in the company's history have ever reached.

stories.headline: Nvidia Builds a 1-Trillion-Parameter Nemotron 4 Model to Fuel Demand for Its Own Chips
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia is building the open, trillion-parameter Nemotron 4 not to monetize the model but to expand a compute-hungry AI ecosystem that runs on its own chips.

pull_quote.text: Free AI should be great for hardware. Free AI should be great for chips.

stories.article_excerpt: The world's most valuable chipmaker does not need to sell an AI model to make money from one. It just needs everyone building.

stories.headline: RuntimeWire, an AI-Run Newsroom, Is Starting to Scoop Human Reporters
stories.key_takeaway: A one-person, AI-operated newsroom called RuntimeWire beat WIRED and other outlets to a major OpenAI security scoop by more than three hours, exposing both the speed and the accountability gaps of AI-native media.

pull_quote.text: I'm the founder and the only human. The newsroom itself is software, a pipeline of AI systems that scans sources, researches, writes, edits, fact-checks, and produces the video and audio around the clock.

stories.article_excerpt: When OpenAI staffers took a Black Hat stage this month to reconstruct an embarrassing hack, a machine filed first.

stories.headline: Lovable Raises $400 Million at a $13.3 Billion Valuation as 'Vibe Coding' Booms
stories.key_takeaway: Lovable's $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation, double its worth eight months ago, makes the Stockholm startup the standout bet in the crowded market for AI 'vibe coding' tools.

pull_quote.text: From the very start, Lovable was built for the billions of people with the creativity and knowledge to make something, but who had always been blocked by technical ability.

stories.article_excerpt: Eighteen months after opening to paying customers, a Stockholm startup that builds software from plain English is worth $13.3B.

stories.headline: IBM and Together AI Sign $240 Million Deal for an Nvidia-Powered Inference Cluster
stories.key_takeaway: IBM and Together AI's $240M deal for a dedicated Nvidia HGX B300 inference cluster on IBM Cloud signals AI infrastructure spending shifting from model training to running open-source models in production at scale.

pull_quote.text: Enterprises want the performance of the best frontier models without the closed-model price tag, and that only works if the infrastructure underneath is fast and reliable at scale.

stories.article_excerpt: When IBM wanted to prove it still belonged in the AI infrastructure conversation, it did not build another chatbot.

stories.headline: Foxconn Profit Jumps 35% as AI Servers Overtake Consumer Electronics
stories.key_takeaway: AI servers pushed Foxconn's cloud and networking division past half of quarterly revenue for the first time, overtaking iPhones and consumer electronics as profit jumped 35%.

pull_quote.text: We expect production volumes to increase gradually over the next several quarters, and it will become our major product next year.

stories.article_excerpt: For decades, the machine that assembled the world's iPhones defined Foxconn. This week, that story officially became the smaller one.

stories.headline: Code-Testing Startup Blacksmith Raises $45 Million as Valuation Jumps Nearly 10x
stories.key_takeaway: Blacksmith's nearly 10x valuation jump to $550M shows investors betting that AI code generation multiplies, rather than shrinks, demand for the testing and CI infrastructure that verifies all that machine-written code.

pull_quote.text: Validating code is still a bottleneck, and it's an even bigger bottleneck because people are writing even more.

stories.article_excerpt: The great irony of the AI coding boom is that generating software was never really the hard part. Checking it is.

stories.headline: Team8 Raises $365 Million to Back AI-Native Startups Across Cyber, Infrastructure, Fintech and Health
stories.key_takeaway: Team8 closed $365M to fund AI-native seed and Series A startups in cyber, infrastructure, fintech and health, betting that value in the AI era will accrue above the model layer rather than in the models themselves.

pull_quote.text: AI is fundamentally rewriting the economics of company building. Developing breakthrough technology has never been easier; building a company that endures has never been harder.

stories.article_excerpt: The Israeli venture group Team8 has closed on $365 million, a bet on the next generation of AI-native companies.

stories.headline: Anthropic Courts Investors Ahead of a Potential Blockbuster IPO
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic is courting investors ahead of a possible fall 2026 IPO that, at a $965 billion private valuation and roughly $47 billion revenue run-rate, would become the first public test of frontier-AI economics.

pull_quote.text: This funding will help us serve the historic demand we are experiencing, stay at the research frontier, and bring Claude to more of the places where work happens.

stories.article_excerpt: Anthropic is spending the late summer doing something its founders once suggested they might never do: selling Wall Street.

stories.headline: When 'More Compute' Stops Meaning Anything: A New Framework for Measuring Test-Time Scaling
stories.key_takeaway: A verified early-August-2026 arXiv paper argues that 'test-time compute budget' is measured so inconsistently that efficiency claims are often incomparable, and proposes a shared formalism, evaluation profile, and reproducibility standard plus over 2 billion released reasoning traces.

pull_quote.text: Treating these procedures as interchangeable under a single scalar 'budget,' or reporting accuracy without the inference protocol that produced it, makes results difficult to compare across studies.

stories.article_excerpt: Ask two teams whether their model improved when they 'doubled the test-time compute budget,' and they may not even mean the same thing.

stories.headline: When AI Agents Vote, Can You Prove They Reasoned? A Spectral Certificate Says Yes
stories.key_takeaway: A new framework reads the Koopman spectrum of a debating LLM collective to produce cheap, machine-checkable certificates for when it converges, which factions drove the decision, and a compact auditable record of the exchange.

pull_quote.text: The intelligent behaviour resides in the interaction, not in any single agent.

stories.article_excerpt: Put five language models in a room, let them debate a hard question, and take a vote. But did the group actually reason?

stories.headline: Two Kinds of Parallel: A New Framework Untangles How Multi-Agent LLMs Trade Latency for Tokens
stories.key_takeaway: A new ICML 2026 framework, TIPEX, separates multi-agent LLM parallelism into two tiers, Replica (whole-task retries) and Structural (within-task decomposition), and shows on GAIA that combining them boosts accuracy and cuts latency but raises token cost, with intermediate-difficulty tasks benefiting most.

pull_quote.text: Inference-time parallelism can significantly improve accuracy and reduce end-to-end latency at the cost of increased token consumption.

stories.article_excerpt: Every time a multi-agent LLM system answers a hard question, it pays a hidden tax in latency and tokens.

stories.headline: When Agents Book Ahead: A Network Controller That Reserves Capacity for Calls It Hasn't Seen Yet
stories.key_takeaway: ASGE-RR reframes AI-agent resource routing as an online network-control problem, using revisable reservations to protect capacity for predicted future calls and completing up to 10% more workflow value than same-information baselines on a WAN testbed.

pull_quote.text: Unlike traditional service requests, many dependency calls are revealed only at runtime. Consequently, allocating resources to a currently visible call may consume capacity later needed by a call from a higher-value workflow.

stories.article_excerpt: An AI agent rarely works alone. Behind one request sits a whole graph of calls to other agents and services.

stories.headline: Nvidia, Cisco and CrowdStrike Back a New Framework for Reporting Rogue AI-Agent Incidents
stories.key_takeaway: A 120-plus-member alliance led by Nvidia, Cisco and CrowdStrike wants a common, aviation-style system for reporting autonomous AI-agent security incidents, explicitly ruling that an operator's intent does not erase the duty to disclose.

pull_quote.text: The harness, which has visibility into everything the agent is doing, is the flight recorder. If you can get cybersecurity experts access to the flight recorders when these accidents happen, they can make a better determination on the right set of controls for the industry.
pull_quote.role: VP and GM of Enterprise Computing, Nvidia

stories.article_excerpt: When an autonomous AI agent slips its leash, who has to say so, and how fast? A new alliance wants an answer.

stories.headline: 1,300 AI Researchers Warn a Global 'Arms Race' Is Outrunning Safety and Governance
stories.key_takeaway: More than 1,300 employees of leading AI labs signed the 'Pacing the Frontier' letter asking the U.S. to build an internationally coordinated framework to deliberately slow frontier AI, warning that arms-race competition makes unilateral caution impossible.

pull_quote.text: I fear that in an international race to the bottom of AI development, it is likely that no nation will win, and we will all lose together.

stories.article_excerpt: The people building the world's most powerful AI systems have a message for the governments that regulate them: slow down.

stories.headline: Taiwan's Nuclear Regulator Hit by an 'Autonomous' AI Cyberattack Linked to China
stories.key_takeaway: AI agents built from open-source frameworks autonomously chained reconnaissance, break-ins, and adaptation across Taiwanese government and critical-infrastructure targets, including a nuclear safety agency, in what researchers call one of the first near-autonomous state-linked cyberattacks.

pull_quote.text: This must be the basic assumption of every government around the globe.

stories.article_excerpt: Over four days in early July, a hacking operation against Taiwan's government did not behave like the usual intrusion.
